results.text:
Flamingo Raises $4.5 Million to Automate MSP Operations | TMC Insight

# Flamingo Raises $4.5 Million to Automate MSP Operations

 Rich Tehrani · TMC Insight • September 4, 2026 

### Key Takeaways

- Vertex Ventures led Flamingo’s $4.5 million seed round.
- Flamingo uses AI agents to reduce labor-intensive MSP support and security work.
- Adoption will depend on integration depth, governance, and measurable margin improvement.

Flamingo is betting that artificial intelligence can change the economics of managed IT services, not merely add another assistant to the help desk. The startup has secured a $4.5 million seed round led by Vertex Ventures to develop an AI-driven platform for managed service providers, or MSPs, according to Reuters.

MSPs run technology environments for businesses that lack large internal IT departments or prefer to outsource day-to-day operations. Their work can cover user support, device management, identity, cloud administration, monitoring, and cybersecurity. It is a large market, but often an operationally awkward one. Providers may rely on separate systems for ticketing, remote management, documentation, endpoint security, billing, and alert handling.

The San Francisco startup secured seed funding from Nexus Venture Partners to build analytics and optimisation tools for software sold to AI agents.

 By The Datatech Times Editorial Team Thu, 10 September 2026

 

Lightsage, a San Francisco startup founded by Jun Liang Lee and Sean Er, has raised $4 million in a seed round led by Nexus Venture Partners. The company is building what it calls an Agent-Led Growth (ALG) platform: infrastructure that helps software vendors understand how AI coding agents discover, evaluate and use their products, rather than optimising solely for human buyers.

results.author: Jesse Landry
results.text:
BoomerangHR Raises $12.7M for Employee Alumni AI | DevCuration

September 15, 2026

• Jesse Landry

# BoomerangHR Raises $12.7M for Employee Alumni AI

Companies spend years learning how an employee performs, collaborates, recovers from mistakes, and navigates the business. When that person leaves, much of the useful record usually collapses into an exit form, a disabled email address, and somebody's memory.

BoomerangHR has raised a $12.7M seed round around the value employers lose in that handoff. Kalos Ventures and Album Ventures co-led the financing, with Monta Vista Capital, Capital Eleven, and Strada Education Foundation participating. The company announced the round on September 14, 2026, as it emerged from stealth with software for offboarding and corporate alumni management.

The broader bet is that former employees are becoming a more important source of trusted talent while the external hiring funnel becomes easier to flood and harder to verify. BoomerangHR wants to turn an employer's alumni history into a working system for rehires, referrals, and commercial relationships instead of leaving those connections to chance.
